title: Kernel multiplexing and eviction strategy + warmup harness for attention runtimes
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: recent integration of FlashAttention v3 improved best-case throughput but introduced brittle memory behavior and p95 jitter across mixed-sequence workloads. We need a runtime-level approach that: 1) safely multiplexes attention kernels for concurrent requests with diverse sequence lengths/precision, 2) evicts or compacts intermediate kernel state to prevent transient OOMs, and 3) provides a deterministic warmup/warm-cache harness to avoid cold-start regressions during rollouts.

Goal: implement a kernel multiplexing queue keyed by (model-variant, seq_bucket, precision) with a lightweight eviction policy and a warmup harness that preloads hot kernels during canary rollouts. Deliverables: design doc, microbench harness, CI regression suite, implementation + canary rollout, and rollback/fallback paths to FlashAttention v2 if symptoms appear. Acceptance criteria: p95 latency regression <=5% vs baseline for 95% of workload shapes and no increase in OOMs in canary cluster; automated regression tests added to CI and a console alert if eviction rate >0.5% over 10 minutes.
work_log: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: scoped work with infra and serving teams; confirmed memory spike reproducer from customer trace (trace id: trace-2301). Decided on multiplexing keyed by seq_bucket and precision instead of per-request kernel instantiation to reduce allocation churn.

2026-03-03 - Prototype: implemented in local branch (github.com/redwood-inference/inference/PR-2148) a naive multiplex queue with size cap. Initial microbench (seq=1024,batch=1,fp16) shows 9% throughput improvement but 12% p95 jitter on mixed seq workloads.

2026-03-05 - Investigation: observed that large sequence evictions caused memory compaction which blocked CUDA streams and spiked latency. Reproduced on dedicated p4d node. Profiling: eviction GC takes ~40ms and correlates with p95 spikes.

2026-03-07 - Trade-offs discussion: Options considered: synchronous eviction (simple, causes stalls), background compaction thread (complex, risks stale pointers), soft-eviction (LRU mark + lazy free on low-pressure). Chosen: soft-eviction with per-stream free lists to avoid cross-stream synchronization.

2026-03-08 - Warmup harness: designed a warmup runner that replays representative traces (seeded from recorded customer traces + synthetic shapes). Warmup runs in canary before traffic switch to populate KV caches and precompile/select kernels.

2026-03-09 - Safety net: added automatic fallback policy: if canary OOMs or p95 regresses beyond threshold, traffic switches to v2 kernel binary for that model-variant for 10 minutes and paging is disabled. Documented fallback in rollout runbook.

2026-03-10 - Benchmarks: microbench results attached show tail latency improvements for long-seq heavy workloads but a small regression for many short-seq low-batch workloads. Plan: refine seq_bucket boundaries and add a fast-path for seq<=64 to prefer v2 kernels.

2026-03-11 - Code review: PR-2159 created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/2159). Feedback from Samir Gupta: clarify ownership of per-stream free list lifecycle and add metrics for eviction_latency, eviction_count, kernel_switch_count. Diego to address comments.

2026-03-12 - CI: added attn-kernel-smoke test to nightly that runs recorded traces with quantized/float variants and asserts no OOMs and p95 within thresholds. Initial CI run passed on linux-gpu-2 but flagged a memory leak in mixed-precision path — tracking in ENG-90201.
comments: Diego Morales (2026-03-04): Prototype looks promising. Need to add metrics before merging; suggest eviction histogram and per-bucket hit-rate. Also add an opt-out flag for customers who need deterministic v2 behavior.

Priya Nair (2026-03-06): Design concern: ensure warmup harness does not leak user data. Confirmed warmup will use synthetic and anonymized traces only, and we will run under canary ML tenant with strict logging controls.

Samir Gupta (2026-03-11): Code review: ensure the per-stream free list ties lifecycle to stream destruction; otherwise we leak when streams are long-lived. Also request test coverage for interleaved prefill+decode workloads.
Ava Patel (2026-03-12): Added CI smoke test. Next: tune seq buckets and rerun distributed stress tests for 48h on dedicated infra, then schedule canary for runtime-1.20-beta cluster.
Diego Morales (2026-03-12): Created rollback playbook entry and console alert rule. Will monitor eviction_rate and p95; if eviction_rate > 0.5% sustained, trigger automated rollback.
